summary: Sheikh Ali Mashhour delivers a comprehensive lecture on modern superstitions through an Islamic lens, continuing a previous series on this topic. The lecture focuses on distinguishing between rare supernatural phenomena like true magic (sihr) and common misconceptions that people attribute to external forces. The Sheikh emphasizes that magic, when it involves worship of other than Allah through interactions with demons, is a major sin and rare occurrence. He explains that humans and jinn are the only creatures with free will, and that jinn are physically powerful while humans are more eloquent. The lecture uses diagnostic logic, comparing superstition to medical diagnosis—just as a person with cold symptoms wouldn't immediately assume cancer, people shouldn't blame all their problems on magic or possession when internal factors are more likely culprits.
